ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.severity: MATERIAL — RECORDED SO THE RECEIPT DOES NOT IMPLY AN ORDERING THAT DID NOT HAPPEN
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.the_contradiction: This task's committed objective (ledger/handoffs/TASK-20260903-bdd0bb.yaml) reads: 'Commit the exact producer artifacts as immutable bytes, ALONE, BEFORE ANY REVIEWER READS THEM.' Its committed `depends_on` in dispatch_queue.json is [TASK-20260903-59e9b9, TASK-20260903-373afa, TASK-20260903-d3bef8, TASK-20260903-9318b5] — and TASK-20260903-373afa and TASK-20260903-9318b5 are BOTH REVIEWERS (role: validator). The queue therefore schedules this snapshot archive AFTER two of the reads it was written to precede.
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.what_this_means_concretely: A snapshot-before-review did NOT occur for the panel or for amendment 005. The T-003/T-004 classification (TASK-20260903-373afa) read the panel before this archive existed, and the T-005 column (TASK-20260903-9318b5) read the panel and amendment 005 before this archive existed. Any later record that cites this receipt as evidence that reviewers read post-snapshot bytes would be wrong.
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.whose_defect_it_is: A CONTRADICTION IN THE BATCH DESIGN, not a departure by the agent executing this task and not a departure by any producer. The objective and the dependency list were both committed before any task in this batch ran.
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.what_is_still_true: The `depends_on` list is correct for a batch-wide content archive of four producers; the objective sentence is correct for a per-producer snapshot gate. What is wrong is that one task was given both jobs. The gate the reviewer cards cite (this task's declared `uncertainty_reduced`: 'Whether the gates the reviewer cards cite are committed when issued') is therefore NOT discharged by this archive as designed.
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.not_repaired_here: The queue and the handoff are committed records and are immutable. No edit to either is made or proposed. The repair, if any, is a new record: routed to the Coordinator decision closing BATCH-ae07ce.
ordering_defect_in_this_tasks_own_placem.the_generalisable_lesson_for_the_next_ba: A snapshot archive whose depends_on includes its own downstream reviewers cannot be a snapshot-before-review. Either the archive is split into per-producer snapshots that depend only on their producer, or the objective drops the before-any-reviewer clause and the batch relies on the preservation-commit discipline recorded in the next block.

what_actually_protected_the_bytes.the_honest_description: PRESERVATION COMMITS, NOT A SNAPSHOT RECEIPT. Each producer artifact was committed the moment its task returned, before the next task started. The reviewed bytes ARE pinned in git history; they are pinned by those commits rather than by any formal snapshot archive, and this receipt says so rather than describing an ordering that did not occur.
what_actually_protected_the_bytes.cap_on_those_four_shas: REPORTED TO THIS SESSION, NOT VERIFIED BY IT. The verification is owed by the orchestrating session and by the batch validator (TASK-20260903-34d50e).
what_actually_protected_the_bytes.the_one_independent_confirmation_that_ex: The -005 reader (TASK-20260903-9318b5) confirmed FROM ITS OWN SESSION that it read committed bytes: its worktree differed from 85383bc7c by exactly one file, its own claim record. what_actually_protected_the_bytes.what_it_does_and_does_not_establish: IT ESTABLISHES that the -005 reader's inputs were committed when it read them. IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH that a snapshot archive preceded any review, and it does not close the objective this task was given.
what_actually_protected_the_bytes.the_freeze_receipt_dependency_this_leave: TASK-20260903-59e9b9's freeze-receipt.json states that the panel freeze 'binds from the archival snapshot commit of TASK-20260903-bdd0bb' and names as owed by this task the check that the archived tree contains no protocol-amendment-GOAL-AES-002-005 text. binding_mode.why: The default `commit` mode requires the archive commit to change EXACTLY the declared archive and source artifacts. That is unsatisfiable for this batch, and the reason is the ordering defect this receipt already records. Each producer artifact was committed PRESERVATION ONLY the moment its task returned, so by the time the archive commit was made there was nothing left for it to introduce and its diff is the receipt alone. tools/research_dispatch.py rejected it with 'commit must change exactly declared archive and source artifacts (missing [...6 paths])'.
binding_mode.why_this_mode_is_legitimate_here_and_not: content_first is a first-class binding mode in the dispatcher, not a bypass. Its own comment states it 'deliberately binds every declared artifact byte at HEAD instead of insisting that one commit changed the entire source package', and CLAUDE.md makes it the repository's stated philosophy: 'Archive receipts bind to CONTENT first... A content mismatch is still fatal.' It relaxes NOTHING about content: all seven declared paths are still hashed and compared, a real reachable commit and a matching first parent are still mandatory, and the commit message must still carry every record id.
binding_mode.what_is_genuinely_weaker: Under `commit` mode the archive commit itself proves the artifact set was introduced atomically, in one commit, at one moment. That proof is NOT available here and is not claimed. What replaces it is per-artifact preservation commits made as each task returned, plus the -005 reader's independent confirmation that it read committed bytes. Weaker, and recorded as weaker.
binding_mode.root_cause_for_the_batch_close: Committing each artifact on return conflicts with an archive contract that requires the archive commit to be the one introducing them. Both behaviours are individually correct; together they are not. DEC-20260903-9c3e26 should rule on which the harness wants, because every future batch run this way hits it.
